newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended vulnerable but off its worst levels on Tuesday after hitting a new all-time low of 4.6940 bid against the dollar amid ongoing dollar demand from local importers and overseas speculators.

Local traders said a close above 4.6850 was bearish and could signal an assault on the 4.7000 and 4.7250 levels on Wednesday despite perceptions that the currency's moves over the last few days had been overdone.
The rand ended the day at 4.6865/15 on the dollar after an intraday worst bid of 4.6940 and from 4.6570/6620 late on Monday.

Against the British pound, it sank to another record low of 7.5432 bid, but crawled off its weakest levels towards the close. It was last at 7.5406/5529 from Monday's 7.5173/5300 while on the mark it was quoted at 0.3220/3226.
Currency dealers said trade had been choppy and the Reserve Bank had shown its hand in the market throughout the day.
"The Reserve Bank was more aggressive than in the past and showed significant efforts in pushing the rand lower," one trader at a large commercial bank said.
Dealers said the rand would likely test the higher 4.70 levels over the next few days, depressed by continuous dollar demand.

"The guys are nervous out there and therefore moves appear to be very quick. Everyone is covering left, right and centre and if there are no signs of a retracement we could target 4.7250 tomorrow (Wednesday)," one said.
The rand's most recent slide was triggered by concern at the worsening inflation picture, high credit growth and downbeat remarks by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals.

On the bond market, yields slavishly followed the rand with the yield on the benchmark R150 bond hitting a five-month high of 16 percent bid on the back of fresh selling but retracing to close below the figure.
Bond dealers said the market was "100 percent rand-driven" and had ignored bullish U.S. Treasuries.
"We saw some buying at the 16 percent figure but it was mainly driven by option books ahead of the close-out in around 10 days," a bond trader said.
He said market direction would be dictated by the rand and the general feeling was that the 16 percent level could break decisively.
"The 16 percent level is also an option-strike level and the momentum appears upwards," he added.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners remained net buyers on Monday, taking a net 83.88 million rand worth of South African bonds after buying 757,697 rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 5.39 billion rand from 6.03 billion rand on Friday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rate rose to between 16.30 and 16.15 percent from 16.15 and 16 percent on Monday. The 90-day BA rate was also higher at 15.70 to 15.55 percent from 15.55 to 15.40 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.359 billion rand on Monday from 7.386 billion rand on Saturday.
